subject: Transportation Systems
title: Cut-and-Cover Construction
description: Learn Cut-and-Cover Construction in one minute.

hook.text: The simplest way to build a subway is the messiest: dig a trench, lay tracks, and cover it up.

buildup.text: Cut-and-cover rips up entire streets. Traffic stops, pipes get rerouted, and neighbors lose patience.

discovery.text: But it's cheap and fast. Most early subways—London, New York, Paris—were built this way.

twist.text: The tunnels sit just below the surface, so stations need fewer stairs and no deep escalators.

climax.text: Modern cities still use cut-and-cover for shallow sections, pairing it with boring machines for depth.

punchline.text: Sometimes the best engineering is just a bigger shovel.
